nginx-certificate-generator.name: Nginx certificate generator

online.intro: Get a free Let's Encrypt certificate after proving DNS control. The server generates the private key and includes it in the Nginx ZIP.
online.disabled: Online issuance is not enabled here. Use the Certbot guide or ask your administrator.
online.staging: Test mode: staging certificates are not trusted by browsers.
online.domainsHint: Enter up to 20 names you control, including any wildcard names. Add the root domain separately if needed.
online.access: Issuance access token from your administrator
online.dnsHint: Add every TXT value below. If two records have the same name, keep both values until issuance is complete.
online.install: The ZIP includes fullchain.pem, privkey.pem and an Nginx configuration snippet. Keep the key private. This certificate does not renew automatically.
online.downloaded: Download started. You can now remove the TXT records for this order.

errors.origin: This site is not configured for online issuance.
errors.busy: The service is busy. Try again shortly.
errors.dns: Not all TXT values are visible yet. Wait for DNS propagation and retry.
errors.expired: The order expired. Create a new one.
errors.rejected: The CA rejected the order. Check DNS and create a new order.
errors.upstream: Issuance could not be completed. Try again shortly.

nginx-certificate-generator.description: Prepare free Let's Encrypt certificates for Nginx, or generate a local self-signed certificate and private key.

meta.title: Free Nginx SSL certificate generator
meta.description: Generate Certbot commands, Nginx HTTPS configuration and renewal steps, or download locally generated self-signed PEM certificates.

nginx-certificate-generator.publicNotice: Public certificates are issued by Let's Encrypt after domain validation on your server. This page prepares commands and configuration; it does not issue a public certificate here.
nginx-certificate-generator.localNotice: Self-signed certificates are for development and testing. Browsers do not trust them by default. Private keys are generated locally, never uploaded or stored, and disappear when you clear or leave this page.
nginx-certificate-generator.platform: Commands target Debian/Ubuntu with systemd and a host-installed Nginx. Review and merge configuration into the appropriate existing virtual host.
nginx-certificate-generator.domainsHint: One name per line, or separate with commas or spaces. First name defines the certificate name. Up to 20 unique names; international names are converted to ASCII. Wildcards require DNS validation and do not cover the root domain.
nginx-certificate-generator.localDomainsHint: DNS names only, including localhost and *.example.test. Add every hostname you will use. IP addresses are not supported by this tool.
nginx-certificate-generator.emailHint: Used by Certbot to register your Let's Encrypt account. It is included only in the commands you copy.
nginx-certificate-generator.httpHint: Point all A/AAAA records to this server and allow inbound port 80. The Nginx plugin requires an existing matching server_name. Webroot requires the HTTP bootstrap configuration below before issuance.
nginx-certificate-generator.dnsHint: Cloudflare must host DNS for all names. On the server, create the credentials file with a token limited to Zone:DNS:Edit and Zone:Zone:Read for the required zones. The token is never entered here. DNS validation supports wildcard names and unattended renewal.
nginx-certificate-generator.staging: Use Let's Encrypt staging to test issuance
nginx-certificate-generator.stagingNotice: Staging certificates are not publicly trusted. After testing, turn staging off and follow the production replacement command shown below.
nginx-certificate-generator.terms: I accept the Let's Encrypt Subscriber Agreement for the account email above.
nginx-certificate-generator.stepIssue: 3 · Request the certificate on your server
nginx-certificate-generator.installHint: Nginx and systemd are prerequisites. The commands install Certbot and the selected plugin; existing package installations should be reviewed first.
nginx-certificate-generator.challengeHint: Save or merge this HTTP server block and reload Nginx before requesting a Webroot certificate. Keep the challenge location in the final HTTPS configuration for renewal.
nginx-certificate-generator.dnsSetupHint: Run these commands interactively on the server, paste the Cloudflare token into the editor, then save. Do not put a real token in this page or in shell history.
nginx-certificate-generator.deployHint: After issuance succeeds, save or merge the configuration below, then run sudo nginx -t && sudo systemctl reload nginx. Certificate files must exist before enabling the TLS server block.
nginx-certificate-generator.renewHint: The deploy hook reloads Nginx only after a certificate is renewed. Check the timer and dry-run result; a failed dry run must be fixed before relying on renewal.
nginx-certificate-generator.bundleHint: The ZIP contains fullchain.pem, privkey.pem and nginx.conf. For the local configuration, place the PEM files in /etc/nginx/ssl/local-test, restrict privkey.pem to mode 600, and validate Nginx before reloading.
nginx-certificate-generator.errorDomains: Enter 1–20 valid DNS names. URLs, IP addresses, ports and shell/configuration characters are not allowed.
nginx-certificate-generator.errorWildcard: Wildcard certificates require Cloudflare DNS validation. Also add the root domain if it needs coverage.
nginx-certificate-generator.errorEmail: Enter a valid email address with an ASCII domain.
nginx-certificate-generator.errorPath: Use an absolute Linux path with letters, numbers, dots, underscores, slashes and hyphens; no spaces or parent-directory segments.
nginx-certificate-generator.errorPort: Application port must be an integer from 1 to 65535.
nginx-certificate-generator.errorTerms: Accept the Subscriber Agreement before preparing an ACME account command.
nginx-certificate-generator.errorDays: Validity must be an integer from 1 to 365 days.
nginx-certificate-generator.errorCrypto: Secure cryptography is unavailable. Open this tool over HTTPS or localhost in a current browser.
nginx-certificate-generator.errorGeneration: Certificate generation failed. Check the inputs and try again.
